source: ACIAR AH/2005/086 'Smallholder Cattle Best Practice Manual' (Windsor, Bush & Young), Best Practice Health and Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia -- hosted at mekonglivestock.wordpress.com (University of Sydney / GDAHP project site)
text: Cattle in Cambodia are commonly housed in pens under the family house or in purpose-built pens nearby, then tethered on rice paddies in the dry season or by the roadside in the wet season (sometimes with access to rice straw), with some farmers still taking cattle to forest land for free grazing. The manual notes that whatever housing system is used, animals need abundant nutrition, plentiful clean water, shade/shelter, and room to move and socialize (so normal heat-related behaviours can occur). It flags that for many large ruminants in Cambodia, neither the housed-tethered system nor free grazing alone provides enough forage to meet energy needs, especially in rice-growing areas where energy deficiency is common; planting dedicated forage is usually needed to close this gap, since without it the majority of cattle remain in poor body condition year-round.
